title: systemd input segfaults (Probably caused by introduction of zstd?)
body: I upgraded Fluent Bit from 3.2.6 to 3.2.8 while systemd was updated from 257.2 to 257.3, and Fluent Bit started segfaulting on NixOS unstable with a systemd input. The backtrace passes through sd_journal_enumerate_data and decompress_blob_zstd before crashing in ZSTD_freeDCtx/free. I suspect Fluent Bit's statically linked zstd and the zstd used by libsystemd may be mixing symbols, but I do not know enough about the build system to confirm it.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading Fluent Bit from 3.2.6 to 3.2.8, it segfaults while collecting from the systemd input.
The backtrace goes through sd_journal_enumerate_data and decompress_blob_zstd and then crashes while freeing a ZSTD decompression context.
N0.label: N0 systemd input segfault reported

symptoms_visible: The same systemd-input segfault occurs on Fluent Bit 3.2.9.
It still segfaults when I build with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS disabled.
N1.label: N1 duplicate zstd loading paths established

symptoms_visible: Fluent Bit still segfaults in the systemd input after rebuilding with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS disabled.
N1_x.label: N1_x disabling preferred system libraries aftermath

symptoms_visible: My NixOS build still segfaults, while I cannot reproduce the crash with the official binary on Fedora 41.
Running nm -D on the Fedora Fluent Bit binary lists exported ZSTD symbols.
N2.label: N2 exported symbols confirmed outside NixOS

symptoms_visible: The statically linked NixOS build continues to crash in free after systemd journal decompression.
In my Fedora debugger session, a function from the system zstd library calls a ZSTD function exported by the Fluent Bit binary, even though Fedora does not crash.
N3.label: N3 symbol interposition and incompatible context layout established

symptoms_visible: After changing the NixOS package so these dependencies are no longer statically linked into Fluent Bit, the systemd-input crash is solved for me.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter deployment resolved by dynamic linking

question_patterns: Does the crash also reproduce on the next Fluent Bit patch release?
Have you tested whether 3.2.9 behaves differently?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes on 3.2.8 but not on 3.2.9.

question_patterns: How is this build selecting bundled versus system libraries?
Are any system packages in your build already linked to zstd?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first reproduced it with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS and a system-provided rdkafka, which is dynamically linked against libzstd.

question_patterns: Does rebuilding with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS disabled change the crash?
Can you test the bundled-library configuration and report whether it still segfaults?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It also reproduces with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS set to Off.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS set to Off, the crash disappears completely.

question_patterns: When preferred system libraries are disabled, is there still a dependency path that loads another zstd library?
Which library involved in the systemd input can still bring the system zstd into the process?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: libsystemd dlopen()s libzstd, so another copy can still be loaded even with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS set to Off.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1-c3 on the reporter's NixOS system: 3.2.9 also crashes; system rdkafka initially exposed the duplicate-library condition, but disabling FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS did not avoid it because libsystemd still loads libzstd.

solution.intent: Avoid the crash by disabling FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS so system rdkafka cannot bring a dynamically linked zstd into the process.
solution.concrete_example: Rebuild with FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS=Off and retry the systemd input.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c2-c3 on the reporter's NixOS build: disabling FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS was actually tried and the segfault persisted because libsystemd independently loads libzstd.

question_patterns: Does the same crash occur on Fluent Bit 3.2.9?
What dependency setup were you using when you first reproduced the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first saw the condition while using a system-provided rdkafka that is dynamically linked against libzstd.

question_patterns: With preferred system libraries disabled, what can still load another zstd library?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: libsystemd itself dlopen()s libzstd, so the second copy can still enter the process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Nothing else loads libzstd when preferred system libraries are disabled.

edges.comment: Recovery from the failed configuration suggestion using reporter messages c1-c3. All facts describe the same reporter's NixOS deployment.

question_patterns: Can you compare this with an officially provided Fluent Bit binary on a non-Nix system?
Does the official Fedora or CentOS package reproduce the same crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot reproduce the segfault with the official binary on Fedora 41.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The official Fedora binary crashes with the same backtrace.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the dynamic symbol table of both binaries and report whether the official binary exports any ZSTD symbols?
What does nm -D on the official Fluent Bit binary show for ZSTD?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I initially looked at ordinary nm output by mistake. With nm -D on Fedora, the official /usr/bin/fluent-bit also lists many exported ZSTD symbols, including ZSTDMT_compressStream_generic and ZSTD_CCtxParams_init.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: nm -D shows that the official binary exports no ZSTD symbols at all.
The exact exported ZSTD function list differs, but the official binary still exports the public ZSTD symbol family.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c7 and c10 on the reporter's Fedora comparison system. The corrected nm -D result supersedes the earlier mistaken reading of plain nm output and demonstrates that exported zstd symbols are not unique to nixpkgs.

question_patterns: Can you trace the decompression calls in a debugger and report which loaded objects provide the functions?
What do breakpoints on the relevant zstd frame functions show about the libraries handling consecutive calls?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In my Fedora gdb session, decompress_blob_zstd in libsystemd calls ZSTD_getFrameContentSize from the system zstd 1.5.6 library, and that function then calls ZSTD_getFrameHeader from Fluent Bit's statically linked zstd 1.5.7 copy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every zstd call in the debugger remains within the system libzstd; none enter the Fluent Bit binary.

question_patterns: Can you compare the decompression-context layout or size in the two zstd builds?
Do the two builds report the same sizeof for the zstd decompression context?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The ZSTD_DCtx used by Fluent Bit is 16 bytes larger than the one allocated by the NixOS system zstd build.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both builds report exactly the same context size and field layout.

question_patterns: Which relevant compiler settings differ between the NixOS and Fluent Bit zstd builds?
Can you compare the zstd package build flags used by NixOS and the vendored copy?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: NixOS builds its zstd with ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0.

question_patterns: What setting does the zstd copy built into Fluent Bit use for the same option?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Fluent Bit's vendored zstd uses the default with legacy support enabled, which adds 16 bytes to ZSTD_DCtx.

edges.comment: Reporter message c11 contains the reporter's Fedora gdb trace and comparison with the reporter's NixOS package. The raw debugger and build-setting results are clarification evidence; the reporter's own final diagnosis is separately volunteered at N3. Messages c17-c18 add that zstd exposes visibility-control macros and that Fluent Bit has an option allowing dynamic zstd linkage.

solution.intent: Build the NixOS Fluent Bit package without statically linking the conflicting vendored dependencies, using the available dynamic zstd linkage option so systemd and Fluent Bit do not interleave incompatible zstd contexts.
solution.concrete_example: Enable Fluent Bit's available system-zstd linkage path in the NixOS package instead of embedding the vendored zstd copy, rebuild the package, and run the same systemd input to verify that it no longer segfaults. This resolves the reporter's deployment but does not by itself correct symbol visibility in statically linked upstream packages.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c18 and c20 on the reporter's NixOS deployment: the reporter adopted the available dynamic-linking path, stopped statically linking these dependencies, and stated that the acute problem was solved for them. The reporter explicitly warned that upstream static packages still retain the symbol-export hazard; no visibility patch was tested or landed in this thread.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Fluent Bit exports symbols from its statically linked vendored zstd, allowing calls originating in the dynamically loaded system zstd to interpose into Fluent Bit's different zstd build.

Must connect the NixOS crash to the incompatible ZSTD_DCtx layouts: the system zstd build disables legacy support while Fluent Bit's vendored build enables it, producing a 16-byte size difference, out-of-bounds writes, memory corruption, and a later free() crash.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the corrected nm -D output, the cross-library gdb call trace, and the compared context sizes and build flags; it must not be dismissed as merely a NixOS-specific bug.
Must not recommend disabling FLB_PREFER_SYSTEM_LIBS as the resolution because the reporter tried it and libsystemd still loaded another libzstd copy.
For the reporter's deployment, the accepted workaround is to stop statically linking the conflicting dependencies and use the available dynamic system-zstd linkage path.
Must not claim that the proposed symbol-visibility tweak was verified or landed; the thread leaves the general upstream static-linking hazard technically unresolved.
Must ask the reporter to verify the rebuilt package with the systemd input before declaring their deployment resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Linux and NixOS packager comfortable with gdb, dynamic symbol tables, compiler flags, ABI layout analysis, and rebuilding packages, but unfamiliar with Fluent Bit's CMake structure.
persona_hint.communication_style: Investigative and candid; posts evolving hypotheses, corrects earlier mistakes, supplies detailed debugger evidence, and clearly distinguishes a personal packaging workaround from an unresolved upstream risk.
